title: Bills of Materials (BOM) and variant handling
description: Configure master product specifications, variant/option handling, multi-level BOMs, revision controls, and new product introductions.

items.name: Custom Master product specifications
items.guidance: Focus: Making a list of items with their names, what they look like, and how we measure them (like weight or size).

items.name: Variant/Option handling
items.guidance: Focus: Listing different versions of a toy or tool, like different colors or sizes.

items.name: Multi-level BOM
items.guidance: Focus: Showing how a big toy is made of smaller parts, and those parts are made of even smaller pieces.

items.name: Revision control
items.guidance: Focus: Keeping track of changes we make to a design over time, like version 1, version 2, and why we changed it.

items.name: Design lifecycle management
items.guidance: Focus: Showing if a drawing is just a sketch, waiting for a boss to check it, ready to use, or too old to use.

items.name: New Product Introduction (NPI)
items.guidance: Focus: The steps to build a brand new product, testing a test model first, and checking everything before making lots of them.
items.notes: Stage-gate approval workflows, engineering changes (ECO), prototype builds, and transition-to-production checks.

title: Estimating & Quotations
description: Handle margins, complex multi-line quoting, pricing agreements, and prospective pipelines.
icon: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M9 7.5L12 10.5M12 10.5L15 7.5M12 10.5V16.5M21 12a9 9 0 11-18 0 9 9 0 0118 0z" /></svg>

items.name: Customer Relationship Mgmt (CRM)
items.guidance: Focus: Keeping a list of customers, their phone numbers, and remembering what we talked about with them.

items.name: Quote Mgmt with quote validity and price agreement
items.guidance: Focus: Telling a customer how much a job will cost, how long that price lasts, and getting a boss to agree to it.

items.name: Minimum order Quantity
items.guidance: Focus: Deciding the smallest number of items a customer must buy at one time (like you must buy at least 5 packs).

items.name: Discount % management
items.guidance: Focus: Giving special lower prices to customers who buy a lot of things, or special friends.

items.name: Sales Process, Pipeline Mgmt
items.guidance: Focus: Checking how many people who ask for prices actually end up buying, and guessing how much we will sell next month.

items.name: Variant Configurator with BOM integration and compatibility rules
items.guidance: Focus: A computer helper that lets customers choose options (like choosing a blue bike with a basket) and makes sure those parts fit together.

items.name: Web-shop & E-Commerce Integration
items.guidance: Focus: Connecting our online shop so orders show up automatically, and showing customers if items are still in stock.

title: Sales Order Processing
description: Automate sales confirmations, compliance, e-commerce imports, and order release criteria.

items.name: Export Regs Compliance
items.guidance: Focus: Following the rules when shipping things to other countries, like paying special cross-border fees.

items.name: Delivery Vehicle Optimisation
items.guidance: Focus: Packing trucks tightly and planning the best paths so we can deliver to many houses on one trip.

items.name: Outlook Integration
items.guidance: Focus: Connecting our system to our email app so we can see customer messages in one place.

title: Production Planning & Scheduling
description: Balance supply and demand, run MRP calculations, and allocate factory resources capacity.

items.name: Demand Forecasting
items.guidance: Focus: Looking at what we sold in the past to guess how many things we need to make for Christmas or summer.

items.name: Material Requirement Planning
items.guidance: Focus: Figuring out exactly what parts we need to buy and make so we don't run out of ingredients.

items.name: Gantt view / Calendar view / Kanban view
items.guidance: Focus: A calendar board where we can drag and drop jobs to see who is working on what.

items.name: Job routing
items.guidance: Focus: Writing down the step-by-step instructions for making something (like step 1: cut, step 2: paint, step 3: dry).

items.name: Forward scheduling
items.guidance: Focus: Planning a project starting today and seeing when is the earliest we can finish it.

items.name: Backward scheduling
items.guidance: Focus: Working backward from the day a customer wants their toy to figure out the latest day we must start making it.

items.name: Capacity planning
items.guidance: Focus: Making sure we have enough machines and people working to finish all our jobs without anyone getting overloaded.

items.name: Advanced Planning & Factory Scheduling (APS)
items.guidance: Focus: A smart scheduling board that knows we only have two hands and can't use a machine if someone else is using it.

title: Purchasing & Stock Control
description: Procure raw items, track stock movements, audit inventory, and rate supplier performances.

items.name: Supplier Assessment & Mgmt (SCM)
items.guidance: Focus: Keeping track of who we buy parts from, how fast they send them, and if they send good parts.

items.name: Estimated number of components in stock – think number of SKUs
items.guidance: Focus: Knowing exactly where every single item is kept in the warehouse (like shelf A, bin 3) and how many we have.

items.name: Critical Stock Alerts
items.guidance: Focus: A system that alerts us (like a blinking light) when we are running low on something so we can buy more.

items.name: E-Procurement Portal Integration
items.guidance: Focus: Letting our computer talk directly to the seller's computer to buy things automatically.

items.name: Purchase order revision
items.guidance: Focus: Writing down when we change a shopping list we sent to a supplier, and when they say they will deliver.

items.name: Purchase price agreement
items.guidance: Focus: Remembering the special prices we agreed to pay for parts so they don't overcharge us.

items.name: Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI)
items.guidance: Focus: Letting the seller check our shelves and send us more items before we even have to ask.

items.name: Purchase price variance
items.guidance: Focus: Checking if we paid more or less for something than we expected, and finding out why.

title: Production Management
description: Release work orders, log shop floor feedback, run CAD/PDM interfaces, and assign step-by-step tasks.

items.name: Shop Floor Data Collection
items.guidance: Focus: Tracking when workers start and stop a job, and how much material gets thrown away.

items.name: Production Feedback
items.guidance: Focus: Using simple touch screens and barcode scanners in the workshop to check off tasks.

items.name: Work order creation
items.guidance: Focus: Giving the makers a sheet of paper that tells them what to build today.

items.name: Work in progress tracking
items.guidance: Focus: Real-time tracking of components at different routing stages, and stage completion updates.

items.name: Work Instructions
items.guidance: Focus: Easy instructions with pictures, warning signs, and checks to help makers do the job safely and correctly.

title: Quality Management System (QMS)
description: Enforce standard quality checkpoints, capture deviations, audit material origins, and coordinate corrective actions.

items.name: Quality control plan
items.guidance: Focus: Checking parts when they arrive, during building, and before they leave to make sure they are perfect.

items.name: Deviation mgmt, CAPA
items.guidance: Focus: Putting bad parts in a 'quarantine' box so no one uses them, and figuring out how to prevent mistakes next time.

items.name: Inspection plan
items.guidance: Focus: Deciding what rules a part must follow to pass the test (like: it cannot be wider than a ruler).

items.name: Root cause analysis
items.guidance: Focus: Playing detective and asking 'why, why, why' until we find out why a part broke.

items.name: Approval workflow
items.guidance: Focus: Getting the inspectors to sign their names on a screen to say a product is safe to sell.

title: Pick, Pack & Despatch
description: Manage pick lists, track carton packs, print label requirements, and manage fleet configurations.

items.name: Export Document Mgmt
items.guidance: Focus: Printing the shipping sheets, customs lists, and other paperwork needed to send packages around the world.

items.name: Vehicle Route Planning
items.guidance: Focus: Putting address stops in order so drivers don't have to drive in circles.

items.name: Delivery Fleet Management
items.guidance: Focus: Keeping our delivery vans working, checking driver licenses, and working with other shipping companies.

items.name: Delivery Route Optimisation
items.guidance: Focus: Updating the map path while driving to avoid traffic jams or closed roads.

items.name: Warehouse heat map
items.guidance: Focus: Drawing a map of the warehouse that shows which aisles are busiest so we can put popular items closer to the door.

title: Field Service
description: Track installations, manage maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) tasks, and coordinate engineering timesheets.

items.name: Field Service Engineer resource mgmt
items.guidance: Focus: Sending the closest and smartest engineer to fix a machine at a customer's house.

items.name: Job card creation and sign off
items.guidance: Focus: Writing down what the engineer fixed, what parts they used, and having the customer sign on a tablet.

items.name: Installation & Commissioning, FATs, SATs
items.guidance: Focus: Checking a customer's house, setting up the machine, testing it, and showing them how to use it safely.

items.name: Risk Assessment RAMS and work permit/approval
items.guidance: Focus: Checking for dangers (like hot pipes or wet floors) and writing down how to stay safe before we start fixing.

items.name: Calibration reports and any other compliant specific reports e.g. IATF 16949 compliance
items.guidance: Focus: Writing safety and tuning reports to prove that our tools work exactly like they are supposed to.

items.name: Field service reports
items.guidance: Focus: A summary paper for the customer showing what we fixed and how to keep it working.

items.name: Manage consumable stock for field service engineers
items.guidance: Focus: Keeping track of small things like glue, screws, and tape that engineers use every day.

items.name: Field service engineer's vehicle stock management
items.guidance: Focus: Making sure each engineer's van has enough spare parts in the back so they don't have to drive back to the warehouse.

items.name: Expense managements
items.guidance: Focus: Keeping receipts for gas, hotel rooms, and meals so the company can pay the engineer back.

items.name: Mobile/tablet access for field engineers
items.guidance: Focus: An app on a phone or tablet that works even without internet so engineers can take photos and check off tasks.

title: Customer/Client Facing Portal (WebTicketing)
description: Provide a portal for raising service tickets, tracking progress, website integration, and managing service contracts.
icon: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d="M16.5 6v.75m0 3v.75m0 3v.75m0 3V18m-9-12h12c1.38 0 2.5 1.12 2.5 2.5v7c0 1.38-1.12 2.5-2.5 2.5h-12A2.5 2.5 0 015 15.5v-7A2.5 2.5 0 017.5 6z" /></svg>

items.name: Option to raise service/job tickets from webticket
items.guidance: Focus: A website page where customers can report a broken item, write what happened, and upload a photo.

items.name: Website integration
items.guidance: Focus: Putting the help screen right on our main website so customers can find it easily.

items.name: User mgmt for webticket login
items.guidance: Focus: Letting customers create usernames, passwords, and choose who else in their office can see their tickets.

items.name: Ticketing queue and work in progress flags
items.guidance: Focus: A progress bar on screen (like: 'We got it', 'We are working on it', 'Fixed!') so customers know what's happening.

items.name: Service contract mgmt/remaining hours mgmt
items.guidance: Focus: Keeping track of how many hours of help a customer has paid for (like a prepaid phone card).

title: HR
description: Administer staffing directories, log skills matrices, track certifications, and record working shifts.

items.name: Timesheets
items.guidance: Focus: Tracking when employees start and finish work each day so we can pay them correctly.

items.name: Skill matrix/organogram
items.guidance: Focus: A list showing what everyone is good at (like who knows how to weld, who knows how to code).

items.name: training mgmt
items.guidance: Focus: Organizing classes to teach workers new skills, and remembering when they need to renew their safety licenses.

items.name: expense tracking
items.guidance: Focus: Tracking money spent by workers on office supplies or client lunches.

title: Integrations
description: Connect with external systems including CRM, Finance, E-commerce, shipping carriers, and payment gateways.

items.name: API Documentation
items.guidance: Focus: A rulebook that shows programmers how to connect other games or apps to our system.

items.name: Outlook Integration
items.guidance: Focus: Syncing calendars and customer emails so we don't miss any meetings or notes.

items.name: CRM system - Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho etc
items.guidance: Focus: Sharing customer lists and sales notes automatically with other popular customer tools.

items.name: Finance Systems eg. Sage, Xero, Quickbooks, etc
items.guidance: Focus: Sending bills and money notes to accounting apps like Sage or QuickBooks automatically.

items.name: E-commerce platforms eg. Shopify, Magento, WooCommerce
items.guidance: Focus: Importing online store orders from online shops like Shopify and updating stock counts automatically.

items.name: Shipping carriers eg. DHL, FedEX, UPS
items.guidance: Focus: Printing shipping labels and sending package tracking links to customers automatically.

items.name: Payment gateways eg. Stripe, PayPal
items.guidance: Focus: Taking credit card payments safely online and checking them off as paid.

title: Dashboards
description: Monitor key performance indicators across stock, sales, production, finance, and overall operations.

items.name: Overview Dashboard
items.guidance: Focus: A main screen showing quick numbers on how the business is doing, like a game dashboard.

items.name: Stock Dashboard
items.guidance: Focus: A screen showing how much our stock is worth and alerts for items that have been sitting on shelves too long.

items.name: Sales Dashboard
items.guidance: Focus: A screen showing how many orders we got this month and what toys or tools are selling best.

items.name: Production Dashboard
items.guidance: Focus: A screen showing if our factory is working fast and how many items are being made right now.

items.name: Financial Dashboard
items.guidance: Focus: A screen showing how much money we made, how much we spent, and our actual profit.

title: Other Questions
description: Address critical operational volumes, terminal counts, licensing requirements, and other scoping details.

items.name: How many customer orders per week/month on average
items.guidance: Focus: Finding out how many orders we get a day so we can make sure our computer is fast enough.

items.name: How many purchase orders per week/month on average
items.guidance: Focus: Writing down how many purchase orders we send to suppliers so we can see how much buying we do.

items.name: How many shop floor terminals
items.guidance: Focus: Counting how many computers we need in the workshop so we can buy enough screens.

items.name: Number of User Licenses required
items.guidance: Focus: Counting how many people will use the software so we can pay for the right amount of keys.

title: Finance
description: Manage financial transactions, general ledger, invoice customizations, tax accounts, budgeting, and payment processing.

items.name: Accounts Payable
items.guidance: Focus: Keeping track of bills we owe to other companies, making sure they are approved, and paying them on time.

items.name: Accounts Receivable
items.guidance: Focus: Sending bills to customers, checking if they paid, and sending reminders if they are late.

items.name: Budgeting / Forecasting
items.guidance: Focus: Guessing how much money we will earn next year and planning how much we are allowed to spend.

items.name: Collections Automations
items.guidance: Focus: Sending automatic emails to remind people to pay their bills, and locking accounts if they are too late.

items.name: Financial Statements
items.guidance: Focus: Printing the main money reports that show exactly what we own and how much we made.

items.name: Invoice Customization
items.guidance: Focus: Changing how our bills look, like adding our logo, adding tax details, and changing the colors.

items.name: Journal Entries
items.guidance: Focus: Writing down edits or fixes in our money books, like when we buy a computer and it gets older/worth less.

items.name: Multi-Entry / Consolidation
items.guidance: Focus: Combining money books from different shops or offices, and handling different currencies like dollars and pounds.

items.name: Payment Processing
items.guidance: Focus: Setting up ways for customers to pay us by bank transfer or credit card online.

items.name: Reconciliations
items.guidance: Focus: Matching our receipts to the bank statement to make sure all the math is correct.

items.name: Payment Scheduling
items.guidance: Focus: Choosing which days to pay our bills in batches so we don't run out of cash.

items.name: Payment Settlements
items.guidance: Focus: Tracking when credit card money actually arrives in our bank account and recording bank fees.

items.name: Payment Batches
items.guidance: Focus: Paying a whole group of suppliers at once by exporting a single payment file to the bank.

items.name: Payment Methods
items.guidance: Focus: Keeping credit card numbers and bank details saved safely so customers can pay easily next time.
